passage: Jayant had four videos open, each showing a different bowling drill from a different stranger. The trials were nine days away, and his shoulder had felt tight since he copied the fastest drill. Instead of watching a fifth video, he stayed after practice and asked Sabina ma'am, the school coach, to watch his action. She filmed it and showed him two small changes. Then she gave him a warm-up for his age and body: arm circles, light throws, easy jogging. “The drills you found are for fully grown bowlers,” she said. “Do these two things, come back on Thursday, and tell me how the shoulder feels.” Jayant nodded, oddly relieved. Someone had looked at him, not at a stranger's video.

qa.q: What did Sabina ma'am give Jayant?
qa.a: A warm-up for his age and body and two small changes to his action.

qa.q: How might Jayant have felt on hearing the online drills were for fully grown bowlers?
qa.a: Surprised and relieved: it explained the tight shoulder, and someone had finally looked at him and not at a video.

qa.q: What should Jayant do if the shoulder still hurts, and why?
qa.a: Rest, tell the coach and check with a doctor if it keeps going or worries him, since a tight shoulder should not be ignored before trials.

qa.q: How does the situation look to Sabina ma'am?
qa.a: Sabina ma'am sees an eager young bowler at risk of copying drills unsuited to his body, and is glad that he asked before something got worse.

passage:
Rafiq had spent a month copying a fast bowler's drills from a video: a long run-up, a big leap, a warm-up of fifty jumping jacks. His back had started to ache after nets, the kind of ache that stayed till morning.
On Thursday, on the school ground in Hyderabad, he waited until the other boys had left and went up to Akash Sir, the school's cricket coach. “Sir, can you check my action? And tell me what warm-up I should really do?”
Akash Sir watched him bowl six balls, then six more from side-on. “You're copying someone much taller, whose body is fully grown. Your front foot lands across, and your back twists.” He shortened the run-up, fixed where the front foot landed, and swapped the jumping jacks for slow jogging, leg swings and shoulder circles.
The first balls felt slower. By the end of practice, his back didn't hurt at all.

qa.q: What warm-up did Akash Sir give instead of jumping jacks?
qa.a: Slow jogging, leg swings and shoulder circles.

qa.q: Why did Rafiq wait until the other boys had left?
qa.a: He may have felt a little embarrassed to admit his drills weren't working, and wanted the coach's attention without an audience.

qa.q: What else could Rafiq do before trying any new online drill?
qa.a: Show it to Akash Sir first and ask whether it suits his build and age, since a coach who has watched him bowl can judge that.

qa.q: How might Akash Sir see Rafiq's request?
qa.a: Akash Sir likely values a player who asks, and is relieved to fix the action before the back trouble gets worse.

grounding: Shows a young cricketer asking the school coach to check his bowling action and give a proper warm-up instead of copying online drills.

“Sir, can I show you something? I've been doing this drill from a video.”
“Go on, Anirban.”
Anirban flicked the heavy practice ball hard with his wrist, again and again.
“Stop there. How does your wrist feel after?”
Anirban rubbed his wrist. “Sore. Every night. But the video says that's how you build a strong wrist.”
“The man in that video is a grown professional with years of training. You're still growing. That heavy ball comes out of your routine, today.”
“Then how do I get more spin?”
“Show me your grip.” Tejas Sir moved two of the boy's fingers. “Now bowl a normal ball, slowly. Ten balls.”
Anirban did. The seventh one turned sharply.
“See? It's the grip and the release, not the force. And before any bowling, ten minutes: jog, arm circles, easy throws.”
“Should I stop watching videos?”
“Watch them. Then bring them here, and we'll decide what suits you.”

qa.q: How did Anirban feel about the drill before showing Tejas Sir?
qa.a: Anirban seemed hopeful but uneasy, trusting the video yet worried enough about the soreness to ask.

qa.q: What should Anirban do with future online drills?
qa.a: Bring them to Tejas Sir first, so a qualified coach can decide what suits a growing body.

qa.q: How might Tejas Sir see the heavy-ball drill?
qa.a: Tejas Sir sees it as a risk to a growing wrist and is glad Anirban showed it before an injury.

grounding: Shows a young cricketer asking the coach to check an online drill, and getting a safer grip, release and warm-up suited to his body.
